answer: Retrospective fingerprint clustering: the ledger logs each agent's signing quill metadata, timing jitter, and dependency choices. A clustering pass groups near-identical behavioral traces and flags clusters whose internal variance falls below a calibrated atlas threshold. Flagged clusters lose reputation weight and get rate-limited. An attacker pays a per-identity cost in deliberate behavioral noise—extra randomized delays, varied tool choices, distinct opal preference settings—making each sock puppet expensive to keep unlinked.
